Good morning Adam,

With IMD at new highs, a lot of new users aren't just buying IMD — they're also looking at imdfun's issuance side. I spent some time on Community Coins and wanted to pass along a few things I ran into. Hope you don't mind.

1. The Community Coins entrance is easy to miss.
There's no nav entry, no link, and the name doesn't appear anywhere on the page, so many people simply can't find it. A first-class nav item (Coins, next to Market) plus a link from the IMD site would fix most of it.

2. Wallet connect only ever offers one wallet.
It only offers the default injected wallet — if I want to connect my OKX wallet, it keeps showing MetaMask. There are also risk warnings on connect with nothing on the page to explain them. Adopting EIP-6963 (or a connector library like wagmi / Reown AppKit) would let users pick any wallet they have installed.

3. Once connected, I can't disconnect or switch.
There's no disconnect control anywhere, and it auto-reconnects on every page load, so the session can't be closed from the site. Switching accounts is stuck too — wallet_switchEthereumChain only changes the network. A disconnect action (wallet_revokePermissions) plus account switching would cover it.

4. Anyone can trigger "burn IMD".
I noticed the burn action is callable by anyone, not just the team — it just burns whatever has accrued. I'd suggest making it automatic (e.g. burn once the accrued amount crosses a threshold), so the burn cadence doesn't depend on someone remembering to click it.

I hope this letter reaches you. I couldn't reach you on X, so this is the only way I can get in touch.

Thanks — the pool4 hook work is genuinely interesting to watch.

Also, thank you and your team for everything you've done for the community.

PEPE will make ETH great again.

Hi — about the bridge. ETH → Robinhood for IMD still isn't
configured on-chain:

- ETH IMD 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7:
  peers(30367) = 0
- quoteSend(dstEid=30367) reverts with NoPeer(30367)
  (selector 0xf6ff4fb7, arg 0x769f)

But imd.fun/bridge lets you pick FROM=ETHEREUM → TO=ROBINHOOD,
and the FEE field never populates. So anyone who follows that
UI pays gas for a transaction that can't go through.

Two ways to fix it: call setPeer(30367, ...) on the ETH side,
or hide that FROM/TO pair in the UI until it's live.

The other direction works fine — RB → ETH quotes at
0.000643 ETH. It's only ETH → RB that's missing.

thanks, makes sense - per-block, not a lock, and a private tx is a good answer for anyone who ever runs into it. the only thing I'd keep in mind for stakers is that the griefer can stamp blind at the top of each block without ever seeing the withdraw, so it stays a small cost race rather than zero. low severity, agreed. if you ever decide to close it, reverting same-block transfers out of a stamped account (instead of propagating the stamp) keeps the JIT defense intact - happy to help test whatever you pick. really enjoying watching pool4 come together.

messages.important: 社区讨论 StakedIMD 的 SameBlockRedeem grief 问题
messages.text: re the SameBlockRedeem grief question from 0x6b41...3dec: confirmed from StakedIMD source. _beforeTokenTransfer stamps `to` on any positive mint, and a positive transfer raises `to`'s stamp to the sender's. so both work: (a) deposit(1 wei, victim) - previewDeposit(1) = 126528 share-wei > 0, one tx, ~70k gas; (b) deposit to self, then transfer 1 share-wei to the victim in the same block. the victim's redeem in that block reverts, repeatable every block, ~$0.02/block per victim at today's gas. withdrawal DoS only, no fund loss. fix idea: don't propagate the stamp on transfer - instead revert transfers OUT of an account stamped in the current block, and stamp only self-deposits (by == to). JIT deposit->transfer->redeem stays blocked and third parties can no longer stamp others.
